html:
Paraguay is a landlocked country in the heart of South America, independent since 1811. It is the one country in the Americas where most people speak a Native language, Guaraní, along with Spanish.

The Guaraní had farmed here for at least a thousand years before the Spanish founded Asunción in 1537. Spanish settlers married into Guaraní families, and in the 1600s and 1700s the Jesuit missions gathered tens of thousands of Guaraní into planned towns.

After independence Paraguay went its own way:

  • José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia ruled as dictator from 1814 to 1840 and sealed the country off from the world.
  • Carlos Antonio López and his son Francisco Solano López opened it again and built an army and railways.
  • In the Paraguayan War of 1864 to 1870, Paraguay fought Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay together. It lost land and a very large share of its people, perhaps more than half, though the numbers are disputed.

Paraguay won most of the disputed Chaco region from Bolivia in the Chaco War of 1932 to 1935. Alfredo Stroessner then ruled as dictator from 1954 to 1989, one of the longest rules in Latin American history. With Brazil it built the Itaipu Dam on the Paraná River, one of the largest power plants in the world, and it was a founding member of Mercosur in 1991.
sum: Paraguay is a landlocked country in the heart of South America, independent since 1811. It is the one country in the Americas where most people speak a Native language, Guaraní, along with Spanish.
